title: Context warmup probe and trace safety guard
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a lightweight context warmup probe and trace safety guard to reduce noisy cold-start traces and to quickly detect malformed/invalid trace headers at the API edge. The probe should: (1) prime per-worker KV caches for common prompt prefixes, (2) exercise kernel-paths used for short-sequence bursts to avoid first-request latency spikes, and (3) validate incoming trace headers and normalize them for downstream propagation. The implementation must be minimal overhead (<0.5% p99 latency increase) and ship as opt-in middleware and SDK hook so Dedicated and Private customers can adopt safely.
acceptance_criteria: Probe can be toggled per-route via Runtime config and per-tenant via metadata
End-to-end e2e test that simulates 1000 cold workers and shows median cold-start latency improvement >= 12%
Header sanitizer drops or rewrites invalid trace IDs and increments a diagnostic metric (trace.header.invalid) visible in console
Instrumentation surfaced via SDK hook documented and sample PR to node/python sdks included
Perf impact on steady-state traffic is <0.5% at p99 (benchmarked on c6-gpu-small)
Rollout playbook with canary gating metrics and automatic rollback thresholds created
comments: 2026-01-29 - Maya Chen: Kicked off spike. Verified warmup approach by pre-populating small KV entries and running microbench. Observed reduced first-token latency on cheap kernels (~9% median improvement) but p99 improvement varied.

2026-02-02 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented middleware prototype (edge-proxy level) that emits a trace.warmup.duration metric and a trace.header.valid boolean. Submitted infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5678

2026-02-04 - Review (Raj Patel): Concerned about memory growth if warmup populates large caches; suggested limit per-worker warm entries and LRU eviction. Action: add sizing controls and per-tenant budget.
2026-02-06 - Design note (Sofie Müller): Warmup should focus on common short prefixes for chat join flows. Uploaded Confluence doc with recommended prefixes and sampling strategy.

2026-02-08 - Perf results: End-to-end benchmark on 128-worker cluster with synthetic join traffic: median first-token -14.2%, p99 -9.1%. Need to tighten p99 by reducing contention during warmup. Next: explore staggered warmup and jittered prefetch.

2026-02-10 - Security review requested: header sanitizer rules reviewed; decided to canonicalize trace-id format and drop oversized baggage keys. Security asked for a unit test suite for header parsing edge-cases.
2026-02-12 - Liam O'Connor: Added canary rollout plan and Grafana dashboard panels for trace.header.invalid and trace.warmup.duration. Preparing SDK sample in node SDK on branch feature/ctx-warmup.
2026-02-12 - Ops note: Add alert if trace.header.invalid rate > 0.1% sustained over 5m during canary; alert will pause rollout.
